metadata.title: Effect of school climate on fourth-grade students’ science achievement in the United Arab Emirates: Insights from the 2023 TIMSS Dataset
metadata.venue: International Journal of Educational Research Open

confounders_identified: language of the test spoken at home
extraction.outcome_summary: Using TIMSS 2023 cycle data for fourth-grade students in the UAE, the study examined whether three school-climate domains (social interaction and relationships, sense of physical and emotional safety, and values and beliefs/attitude toward science) were associated with and predicted science achievement. The three domains were correlated with each other and jointly explained a modest share of variance in science achievement, with social and emotional safety contributing most uniquely. Moderation analyses indicated that demographic variables (notably absenteeism and number of books at home) moderated the relationships between school-climate domains and science achievement, with effects varying by moderator category. Missing data were handled via expectation-maximization, and the study used the five TIMSS plausible values by summing them into a single achievement measure.
